properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of north central Montana, including the following
areas, East Glacier Park Region, Eastern Glacier, Western Toole,
and Central Pondera, Eastern Pondera and Eastern Teton, Eastern
Toole and Liberty, Northern High Plains, Southern High Plains and
Southern Rocky Mountain Front.

streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and
streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage areas. Rural gravel and dirt roads can become muddy and
may become difficult to travel. Rock/debris slides are possible in
the mountains.

per hour rain rates. Periods of moderate to heavy rainfall will
be possible Monday through Tuesday morning. Widespread 0.75 to

Front over the past 24 hours. Additional widespread rain
accumulations of 1 to 3 inches are possible along the Rocky
Mountain Front and Sweet Grass Hills with isolated 4 inches
possible along and north of US Highway 2 this afternoon through
Tuesday morning.

properties.instruction:

properties.description:
HLSHFO

This product covers the Hawaiian islands

**TROPICAL STORM WARNING ISSUED FOR KAUAI AND NIIHAU**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- The Tropical Storm Watch has been upgraded to a Tropical Storm
Warning for Kauai East, Kauai Mountains, Kauai North, Kauai
South, Kauai Southwest, and Niihau

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Kauai East, Kauai
Mountains, Kauai North, Kauai South, Kauai Southwest, and Niihau

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 580 miles south-southwest of Lihue
- 14.7N 163.8W
- Storm Intensity 125 mph
- Movement North-northwest or 335 degrees at 6 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------
At 5 am HST, the eye of major Hurricane Lowell was located about
580 miles south-southwest of Lihue. Lowell has maximum sustained winds
of 125 mph, and is now moving toward the north-northwest at 6 mph.
Lowell is expected to continue to turn more toward the north-northeast
tonight into Monday while accelerating. Some fluctuations in
intensity are expected in the short term, with gradual weakening
expected into Monday. A faster rate of weakening is expected by Monday
night and Tuesday due to an increase of vertical wind shear and dry
mid level air. The eye of Lowell is currently forecast to make it's
closest approach to the main Hawaiian Islands Monday night, passing
100 to 200 miles west of Niihau.

Strong, gusty winds on the eastern side of Lowell's circulation are
expected to affect Kauai and Niihau as Hurricane Lowell passes. Winds
will increase on Monday as the hurricane approaches the western end of
the chain. Based on the current forecast, tropical storm force winds,
sustained 39 mph or higher, is expected Monday afternoon. Plan to have
your preparations for damaging winds complete before midday Monday, with winds
peaking Monday night. Even higher gusts, 60 mph or more, are possible
over Kauai and Niihau where winds are accelerated by terrain.

Starting later today, a very large shield of deep tropical moisture
surrounding Lowell will spread northward over the main Hawaiian
islands from south to north, bringing increasing showers. Squally
downpours could lead to flash flooding, along with mudslides in steep
terrain. Rainbands could become persistent and anchored in some areas,
which would exacerbate the flash flood threat. The risk of flash
flooding and mudslides is greatest for Kauai and Niihau, but also
exists for other islands as well due to the extent of the moisture
associated with Lowell. Over a foot of rain is possible over portions
of Kauai, mainly over the interior mountains.

Surf is expected to increase quickly on south and west facing shores
tonight, reaching warning levels by Monday. Damaging surf and some
coastal inundation are expected along the immediate coast on exposed
south and west facing shores on Kauai and Niihau Monday and Monday
night, before diminishing on Tuesday. Highest surf heights in those
areas may reach 20 to 30 feet, along with 1 to 3 feet of coastal
inundation.

Conditions will become favorable for fast-moving, short-lived
waterspouts and tornadoes in the rainbands associated with Lowell,
mainly near Kauai and Niihau, later on Monday. This threat will
continue into Monday night, then diminish quickly Tuesday morning.


POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Prepare for hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
Kauai and Niihau. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

If you are relocating to safe shelter, leave as early as possible.
Allow extra time to reach your destination. Many roads and bridges
will be closed once strong winds arrive. Check the latest weather
forecast before departing and drive with caution.

If heading to a community shelter, become familiar with the shelter
rules before arrival, especially if you have special needs or have
pets. Take essential items with you from your Emergency Supplies Kit.

Failure to adequately shelter may result in serious injury or loss of
life. Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with any
orders that are issued. Remember, during the storm 9 1 1 Emergency
Services may not be able to immediately respond if conditions are
unsafe. This should be a big factor in your decision making.

can be helpful, but be aware of your risk for deadly carbon monoxide
poisoning if your car is left idling in a garage or other poorly
ventilated area.

It is important to remain calm, informed, and focused during an
emergency. Be patient and helpful with those you encounter.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Storm surge is the leading killer associated with tropical storms and
hurricanes! Make sure you are in a safe area away from the surge
zone. Even if you are not in a surge-prone area, you could find
yourself cutoff by flood waters during and after the storm. Heed
evacuation orders issued by the local authorities.

Rapidly rising flood waters are deadly. If you are in a flood-prone
area, consider moving to higher ground. Never drive through a flooded
roadway. Remember, turn around don't drown!

If a Tornado Warning is issued for your area, be ready to shelter
quickly, preferably away from windows and in an interior room not
prone to flooding. If driving, scan the roadside for quick shelter
options.

If in a place that is vulnerable to high wind, such as near large
trees, a manufactured home, upper floors of a high-rise building, or
on a boat, consider moving to a safer shelter before the onset of
strong winds or flooding.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 6 at 10:45AM AST until September 6 at 5:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat can affect anyone without effective
cooling and/or adequate hydration.

* WHERE...Puerto Rico.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during
periods of very high heat indices or high temperatures. This
extreme heat event poses a severe threat to anyone with inadequate
cooling or hydration. These extreme impacts will be most pronounced
across coastal sections, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban
areas.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.description:

MONDAY NIGHT...

surf elevated above High Surf Advisory conditions across south-
and west-facing shores through Monday night. The northward turn

quickly on Tuesday. A large, medium-period east swell from

warning levels. High surf will coincide with monthly high tides,
creating the potential for impacts to harbor entrances,
channels, as well as vulnerable coastal properties and
infrastructure including roadways.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 5 at 8:10PM PDT until September 8 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 5 to 8 feet with local sets to 10 feet and dangerous
and potentially life threatening rip currents, largest on
south- facing shores.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents will be widespread and very strong, potentially
pulling swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves
can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and
capsize small boats near shore. Enhanced beach erosion will
occur. Flooding of sea water is likely, around the time of
high tide, over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas such as
parking lots, beaches, and walkways. Areas most susceptible to
coastal flooding will include Avalon, Long Beach (Alamitos
Peninsula), and Oxnard to Malibu (including Point Mugu).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will occur around 6.7 feet at
6pm on Sunday, 7 feet at 7pm on Monday, and 7.2 feet at 8pm on
Tuesday.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks. Follow advice from local
officials. Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

drainage areas. Those recreating in the backcountry should take
caution on backcountry roadways for falling debris.
